ucs.title: [LLM] APT32 (OceanLotus / Canvas Cyclone) watering-hole → browser-spawned mshta/rundll32 loader
ucs.description: Hunts APT32's signature strategic-web-compromise chain: a compromised news/government site profiles the visitor in JavaScript, then forces the browser to spawn mshta.exe, rundll32.exe, regsvr32.exe or powershell.exe with an HTTP/HTA/encoded-command argument to fetch the next-stage payload (Denis/KerrDown/Cobalt Strike Beacon). The browser→signed-LOLBin transition with a remote URL is rare on production endpoints and characteristic of OceanLotus drive-by delivery.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","opera.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") by host, user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.process_path, Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(https?://|\.hta\b|javascript:|-EncodedCommand|\-enc\s|DownloadString|-w\s+hidden|-WindowStyle\s+Hidden|\\AppData\\|\\ProgramData\\|\\Temp\\)") AND NOT match(user, "(?i)(\$$|SYSTEM|LOCAL SERVICE|NETWORK SERVICE)") | rename firstTime AS first_seen lastTime AS last_seen | convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen) | sort - last_seen
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let Browsers = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","opera.exe"]);
let Lolbins  = dynamic(["mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (Browsers)
| where FileName in~ (Lolbins)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://",".hta","javascript:","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","DownloadString","-w hidden","-WindowStyle")
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\\(Users\\[^\\]+\\AppData|ProgramData|Temp|Public)\\"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Hits=count(),
            SampleParentCmd=any(ParentCmd), SampleChildCmd=any(ChildCmd)
            by DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage, ChildImage, SHA256
| order by LastSeen desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let Browsers = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","opera.exe"]);
let Lolbins  = dynamic(["mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentName = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend ChildName  = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,    "\\")[-1]))
| where ParentName in (Browsers)
| where ChildName  in (Lolbins)
| where CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://",".hta","javascript:","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","DownloadString","-w hidden","-WindowStyle")
   or CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\\(Users\\[^\\]+\\AppData|ProgramData|Temp|Public)\\"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where SubjectUserName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count(), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine)
            by Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName
| order by LastSeen desc

title: APT32 Watering-Hole Browser-Spawned LOLBin Loader
id: 7f3a8c20-a32a-4711-9a01-uc1browserlolbin
status: experimental
description: Detects browsers spawning mshta/rundll32/regsvr32/wscript/cscript/powershell with URL, HTA or encoded-command arguments — APT32 (OceanLotus / Canvas Cyclone) strategic-web-compromise delivery chain.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1189
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1204.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1218.005
  - attack.t1218.011
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.g0050
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
      - '\opera.exe'
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - '.hta'
      - 'javascript:'
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - '-enc '
      - 'DownloadString'
      - '-w hidden'
      - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
  filter_machine:
    User|endswith: '$'
  condition: parent and child and args and not filter_machine
falsepositives:
  - Browser-launched legitimate installers (e.g. ClickOnce, vendor MSI helpers) using mshta/rundll32 with URLs
  - Internal SaaS apps invoking rundll32 via custom URL protocol handlers
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\MsEdge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\Brave.exe OR *\\iexplore.exe OR *\\IEXPLORE.EXE) @Image:(*\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\RunDll32.exe OR *\\RUNDLL32.EXE OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\RegSvr32.exe OR *\\REGSVR32.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\WSCRIPT.EXE OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\Pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*http\://* OR *https\://* OR *.hta* OR *javascript\:* OR *-EncodedCommand* OR *DownloadString* OR *"-w hidden"* OR *WindowStyle*Hidden*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|iexplore|opera)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|wscript|cscript|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(https?://|\\.hta|javascript:|-EncodedCommand|-enc\\s|DownloadString|-w\\s+hidden|-WindowStyle\\s+Hidden|\\\\AppData\\\\|\\\\ProgramData\\\\|\\\\Temp\\\\)", field=CommandLine)
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName], function={ count() | min(@timestamp) | max(@timestamp) | any(CommandLine) })

ucs.title: [LLM] APT32 (Cobalt Kitty) DLL side-loading via known abused signed binary in user-writable path
ucs.description: Detects APT32's hallmark execution trick from the Cobalt Kitty / OceanLotus campaigns: drop a legitimately signed third-party binary (McAfee mcoemcpy.exe, Symantec RasTls.exe / wsc_proxy.exe, Kaspersky avp.exe, Google goopdate.exe, Microsoft outlook.exe / mscorsvw.exe) into a user-writable folder alongside a hijacked DLL of the same base name, then execute the signed binary so the malicious DLL is side-loaded under the trusted process token. Detect by alerting when these specific binary names execute from anywhere other than %ProgramFiles%.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("mcoemcpy.exe","wsc_proxy.exe","RasTls.exe","goopdate.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe","avp.exe","mscorsvw.exe","ssunloader.exe","icmpsvc.exe","OUTLOOK.EXE","VsTskMgr.exe","AcroRd32.exe") by host, user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_path, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process_path, "(?i)\\\\(Users|ProgramData|AppData|Temp|Public|Downloads|Desktop|Intel|PerfLogs)\\\\") AND NOT match(process_path, "(?i)\\\\Program Files") AND NOT match(user, "(?i)\$$") | rename firstTime AS first_seen lastTime AS last_seen | convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen) | sort - last_seen
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let AbusedBinaries = dynamic(["mcoemcpy.exe","wsc_proxy.exe","rastls.exe","goopdate.exe","googleupdate.exe","avp.exe","mscorsvw.exe","ssunloader.exe","icmpsvc.exe","outlook.exe","vstskmgr.exe","acrord32.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName in~ (AbusedBinaries)
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\(Users|ProgramData|AppData|Temp|Public|Downloads|Desktop|Intel|PerfLogs)\\"
| where FolderPath !contains @"Program Files"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId, LoadedDll = FileName, LoadedDllPath = FolderPath, LoadedDllSigner = InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, LoadedSHA256 = SHA256
  ) on DeviceId, $left.ProcessId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
| where isempty(LoadedDll) or LoadedDllPath == FolderPath
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          LoadedDll, LoadedDllPath, LoadedSHA256
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Hits=count(),
            SampleLoadedDll=any(LoadedDll), SampleDllPath=any(LoadedDllPath)
            by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by LastSeen desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let AbusedBinaries = dynamic(["\\mcoemcpy.exe","\\wsc_proxy.exe","\\RasTls.exe","\\goopdate.exe","\\GoogleUpdate.exe","\\avp.exe","\\mscorsvw.exe","\\ssunloader.exe","\\icmpsvc.exe","\\OUTLOOK.EXE","\\VsTskMgr.exe","\\AcroRd32.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any (AbusedBinaries)
| where NewProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(Users|ProgramData|AppData|Temp|Public|Downloads|Desktop|Intel|PerfLogs)\\"
| where NewProcessName !contains "Program Files"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count(),
            SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleParent=any(ParentProcessName)
            by Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName
| order by LastSeen desc

id: 7f3a8c20-a32a-4711-9a02-uc2sideloadpath
status: experimental
description: APT32 (OceanLotus / Cobalt Kitty) drops a legitimately signed McAfee / Symantec / Kaspersky / Google / Microsoft binary into a user-writable folder alongside a hijacked DLL of the same base name and executes it to side-load the malicious DLL. Detect on the signed binary executing from anywhere other than Program Files.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
  - https://www.cybereason.com/blog/operation-cobalt-kitty-apt
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.t1055.001
  - attack.g0050
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\mcoemcpy.exe'
      - '\wsc_proxy.exe'
      - '\RasTls.exe'
      - '\goopdate.exe'
      - '\GoogleUpdate.exe'
      - '\avp.exe'
      - '\mscorsvw.exe'
      - '\ssunloader.exe'
      - '\icmpsvc.exe'
      - '\OUTLOOK.EXE'
      - '\VsTskMgr.exe'
      - '\AcroRd32.exe'
  selection_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '\Users\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\Public\'
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\Desktop\'
      - '\Intel\'
      - '\PerfLogs\'
  filter_legit_path:
    Image|contains: '\Program Files'
  filter_machine:
    User|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection_image and selection_path and not filter_legit_path and not filter_machine
falsepositives:
  - Vendor installers staging signed payloads in ProgramData before final install
  - Portable AV / Acrobat copies deliberately deployed outside Program Files (allow-list the path)
level: high
